stories.headline: Iranian tanker reported hit near Kharg Island after missile attacks
stories.dek: Iranian media said a tanker was struck near a key oil export island, with explosions heard and the crew evacuating.
paragraphs: Iranian media said an Iranian oil tanker was struck by US forces near Kharg Island on Saturday morning, close to the Strait of Hormuz. Reports said several explosions were heard and the ship was being evacuated. No casualties were reported. The claim came one day after Iran reportedly fired anti-ship missiles in the strait.

The area is one of the world's main energy chokepoints, and Kharg Island is central to Iran's oil exports. Fighting between the US and Iran resumed last Sunday after US strikes on Iranian forces and equipment in and around the strait. Since then, both sides have reported further attacks tied to shipping and military sites.

Much is still unclear. There has been no public comment yet from US or Iranian officials on the reported tanker strike. Iranian media gave no details on the ship's condition, any oil spill, or the exact location of the hit. It is also not clear whether commercial traffic through the strait has been disrupted.
stories.changes: This raises the risk of higher shipping costs and tighter oil flows through a route that affects fuel prices far beyond the Gulf.
stories.unchanged: It does not yet mean the Strait of Hormuz is closed or that a wider regional war has been formally declared.

cover.hook: Explosions were reported near Iran's main oil export island by the Strait of Hormuz

art.label: Silkscreen
art.concept: Draw a large oil tanker at dawn seen from slightly above, close to a low dark shoreline. A bright burst and a column of black smoke rise from the ship's midsection while small lifeboats pull away across flat water. Keep the scene empty of people and other vessels so the single damaged tanker carries the whole story.
art.note: Harsh dawn light, limited reds, blacks, and dirty sea-grey.

stories.headline: Russia rejects Ukraine ceasefire proposal as front-line fighting continues
stories.dek: Ukraine said its Sept. 5-9 ceasefire initiative was not accepted and combat continued along the front on Sept. 5.
paragraphs: Ukraine’s military said fighting continued along the front after Russia rejected a proposed ceasefire for Sept. 5-9. The statement was reported on Sept. 5. The proposal mattered because it would have paused combat for several days, but no halt took effect.

For a newcomer, this means the war’s front line is still active across eastern and southern Ukraine. A ceasefire would require both sides to stop attacks at the same time. If one side refuses, shelling, drone strikes, and ground clashes can continue without a formal pause.

What remains unclear is how the ceasefire proposal was delivered, whether any local pauses were discussed, and whether outside mediators were involved. Ukraine’s statement does not show any change in battlefield conditions yet. It also does not indicate that broader peace talks are close.
stories.changes: For ordinary readers in Ukraine, this means no short pause in front-line combat is taking effect this week.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean the wider war has suddenly expanded or that a full diplomatic process has formally collapsed today.

cover.hook: Ukraine said its Sept. 5-9 truce proposal was rejected and fighting continued

art.label: Wood engraving
art.concept: Draw a long trench line cutting across a bare field at dusk, with one white flag laid folded and unused on the ground beside the parapet. In the distance, small bursts of smoke rise at several points along the horizon, showing that the line never went quiet. No soldiers visible.
art.note: Muted earth tones with a hard red accent; tense, low evening light.

stories.headline: Russian strikes kill four as US envoys prepare Ukraine visit
stories.dek: Ukraine says Russia launched missiles and 167 drones overnight before planned peace talks led by two U.S. envoys.
paragraphs: Russian attacks killed four people in southern Ukraine overnight, hours before U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were expected for talks. Kyiv had said it would pause its own air attacks during the visit and asked Moscow to do the same, but strikes continued across several regions.

The war has lasted four and a half years, and fighting along the front has largely stalled. Both sides have instead stepped up long-range attacks. Ukraine says Russia now uses fast jet-powered drones as well as Shahed-type drones and missiles, making air-raid alarms a routine part of life in Kyiv and beyond.

It is not clear whether the U.S. visit will restart serious peace talks or produce even a short pause in attacks. Russia says it hit industrial plants tied to Ukraine's military production, while Ukraine also struck Russia's Belgorod region. Civilians on both sides remain exposed overnight.
stories.changes: For ordinary people in Ukraine, any diplomatic visit will still unfold under the risk of missiles, drones, fires, and disrupted daily life.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean a ceasefire exists or that the war is close to ending, despite the new U.S. push.

cover.hook: Strikes continued even after Kyiv offered to pause air attacks during the U.S. visit

art.label: Risograph poster
art.concept: Draw a dark apartment block at night with one upper corner torn open by a strike, its rooms exposed like a cutaway. In the sky above, a dense spread of small drone shapes crosses toward the building while a fire crew on the ground stands back behind a hose line, forced to wait for the next wave to pass.
art.note: Night scene, hard reds and black, with harsh emergency light.

stories.headline: US envoys arrive in Moscow as Russia strikes Ukraine
stories.dek: Trump says Washington has a peace idea, but Russia kept up air attacks as his envoys traveled to meet Putin and Zelensky.
paragraphs: A US team led by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner traveled to Moscow on Saturday for talks with Vladimir Putin, then plans to go to Kyiv on Sunday. Donald Trump said they carry a new peace proposal. The trip matters now because fighting is still active and earlier diplomacy has stalled.

Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022 and the war is now in its fifth year. Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelensky, offered a temporary pause in airstrikes during the talks. Russia did not accept that proposal and launched fresh strikes, including one on Kamianske that killed four people and injured five.

It is not clear what the US proposal contains or whether either side will accept it. Ukraine also says Russia is studying possible new northern offensives, though Kyiv sees no new attack force there yet. The main test is whether the meetings produce any real pause in attacks.
stories.changes: For ordinary readers, this means another serious round of US-led talks is underway, but daily violence in Ukraine has not paused for it.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean a ceasefire exists, a peace deal is close, or Russia has agreed to stop its attacks.

cover.hook: US envoys reached Moscow as Russian attacks continued across Ukraine

art.label: Mid-century gouache
art.concept: Draw a dark airport apron at dawn with a small business jet parked in the foreground, its door open and stairs down, while far beyond the runway a city skyline shows two thin columns of smoke rising. The image should hold both diplomacy and war in one scene, with the aircraft still and the distant damage fresh. No people visible.
art.note: Flat, tense shapes; cold grey-blue with one harsh orange fire glow.

stories.headline: Bushfire burns on NSW Central Coast near Pacific Highway
stories.dek: Firefighters are working to contain a blaze that has raised fears it could cross a major road corridor.
paragraphs: A bushfire broke out on the NSW Central Coast on Friday, and firefighters moved to contain it as concern grew that the flames could jump the Pacific Highway. That road is a major north-south route. The immediate focus is stopping the fire from spreading across it.

The Central Coast sits between Sydney and Newcastle and includes bushland close to homes, roads and towns. In Australia, bushfires can move quickly when heat, dry vegetation and wind combine. A fire reaching the Pacific Highway could disrupt travel and make firefighting harder on both sides.

It is not yet clear how large the fire is, what caused it, or whether homes are under direct threat. Authorities have not said if the highway has been closed or if evacuations are needed. Weather and wind will help decide whether crews can hold the fire.
stories.changes: People in or travelling through the Central Coast may face warnings, delays or sudden road changes if the fire spreads.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean the whole Central Coast is burning or that the Pacific Highway has already been cut.

cover.hook: Crews are trying to stop a Central Coast fire from crossing the Pacific Highway

art.label: Pen and wash
art.concept: Draw a stretch of the Pacific Highway cutting across the frame, with dense bush on one side and a low wall of smoke and flame pressing toward the road from the other. In the foreground, a fire truck sits angled on the shoulder with hoses laid out, while the far lanes disappear into haze.
art.note: Dry light, smoky air, muted ochres and grey.

stories.headline: Philippine vice-president posts bail in alleged threat case
stories.dek: Sara Duterte-Carpio appeared at a Manila court after a warrant over remarks about President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and his family.
paragraphs: Philippine Vice-President Sara Duterte-Carpio posted bail at a Manila court on Saturday, one day after a judge issued an arrest warrant. She faces a charge of grave threats over remarks in which she said a hitman would kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, his wife and a congressman cousin if she were killed first.

The case matters beyond criminal court. The same alleged threat is a central part of her Senate impeachment trial, now in its 10th week. If she is convicted there, she could be removed from office and permanently barred from politics, damaging a possible run for president in 2028.

Her lawyer said she appeared voluntarily, so police did not arrest her. Duterte-Carpio has said her remarks were misconstrued, and before entering court she said she feared for her life. It is still unclear how quickly the criminal case will move, or how senators will weigh it in the impeachment trial.
stories.changes: The vice-president now has to fight a criminal case and an impeachment trial at the same time.
stories.unchanged: She remains vice-president for now, and posting bail is not a finding of guilt.

cover.hook: The alleged threat now sits in both a criminal case and an impeachment trial

art.label: Constructivist poster
art.concept: Draw the entrance hall of a courthouse with a single empty defendant's chair in the foreground and a low table holding a small stack of cash and a stamped bond paper. In the background, a set of heavy doors stands half open, with security barriers and tiled floors giving the scene a formal public feel. No faces are visible, and no text appears on any paper or wall.
art.note: Flat political poster style, muted reds and greys, tense but controlled.

stories.headline: Reform pledges £15,000 tax-free allowance within first 100 days
stories.dek: The party says most taxpayers would save about £500 a year, funded by £80bn of spending cuts.
paragraphs: Reform UK says it would raise the income tax personal allowance to £15,000 if it wins the next general election. Robert Jenrick plans to present it as a first-100-days measure at the party conference. Reform says the change would put more cash in workers' pockets quickly.

The personal allowance is the amount people can earn before paying income tax. It has been frozen at £12,570 since 2021, which means more people pay tax as wages rise. Reform says lifting it would remove 2.9 million people from income tax and cost £17.7bn in the first year.

The main question is whether Reform's funding plan would hold up. The party says it would cover the tax cut with £80bn of spending cuts, including welfare, aid, net-zero programmes and civil service costs. Its conference launch also comes as party aides face scrutiny over alleged donation discussions.
stories.changes: If this ever became law, many workers would pay less income tax and some low earners would stop paying it altogether.
stories.unchanged: Nothing changes now: this is a conference pledge from an opposition party, not a Budget or an enacted tax cut.

cover.hook: Reform says raising the threshold would cost £17.7bn in year one

art.label: Cut-paper collage
art.concept: Draw a kitchen table with a weekly pay packet opened beside a household budget notebook. One crisp stack of banknotes sits just above a painted tax line on the table surface, while an eraser has rubbed part of that line away, leaving dust and a clean gap. No words or numbers anywhere in the scene.
art.note: Flat political poster feel, limited colours, firm shapes, slightly tense mood.

stories.headline: Damaging winds tear across Sydney causing widespread destruction
stories.dek: Strong winds hit homes, trees and power lines across Sydney, leaving damage spread through multiple suburbs.
paragraphs: Damaging winds are causing destruction across Sydney, with strong gusts hitting the city and surrounding suburbs. The immediate danger is from wind itself: falling trees, broken branches, damaged roofs and debris thrown into streets. The event is unfolding now, with conditions severe enough to disrupt daily life.

Sydney is used to fast-changing weather, but destructive wind events can cause broad damage in a short time. Winds can bring down power lines, block roads and damage buildings even without heavy rain. For residents, the main risks are travel disruption, power cuts and unsafe conditions around trees and loose objects.

It is not yet clear which areas have suffered the worst damage, how many properties are affected or how long disruptions will last. Authorities may still be assessing roads, transport and electricity networks. Residents will need updated warnings and repair timelines before the full scale of the damage is known.
stories.changes: People across Sydney may need to avoid travel, secure property and prepare for power or transport disruptions today.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean every part of Sydney is devastated or that damage will last beyond the current weather event.

cover.hook: Strong gusts are damaging homes, trees, roads and power lines across Sydney

art.label: Stipple portrait
art.concept: Draw a suburban Sydney street just after a violent gust: one large gum tree split across the road, power lines sagging, roof sheets peeled back on a single house, wheelie bins and branches scattered along the curb. No people present, just the physical force of the wind made visible through what it has moved and broken.
art.note: Grey storm light, sharp contrast, heavy lines and a tense, unsettled mood.

stories.headline: Ukraine refinery strikes push diesel prices to record US highs
stories.dek: Russian diesel exports have been cut as refinery outages spread, lifting fuel costs for trucking, farming, deliveries, and food.
paragraphs: Diesel prices in the United States hit a record $5.85 a gallon this week as Ukraine’s drone attacks shut down a large share of Russia’s refining system. The effect matters now because diesel supplies are tight worldwide, and more refineries in other regions are also offline.

The war has disrupted oil flows before, but refined fuel is now the bigger problem. Russia has halted diesel exports after losing major refining capacity. At the same time, outages in the Middle East and lower refinery use in China have removed more than 10% of global refining capacity.

Prices could stay high through the autumn as some North American refineries enter seasonal maintenance or switch to winter fuel. Some plants may delay repairs, but others will still reduce output. The main unknown is whether Russia restores capacity quickly or Ukraine keeps landing successful strikes.
stories.changes: You may pay more for goods, groceries, shipping, and travel even if you do not buy diesel yourself.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean fuel is physically unavailable in most of the United States or that every pump will run dry.

cover.hook: Refinery damage, not crude shortages, is now driving the latest fuel price surge.

art.label: Technical drawing
art.concept: Draw a long line of heavy trucks at a fuel stop at dusk, but the diesel pump hoses lead back to a refinery skyline in the far distance where several distillation towers are dark and cold. One lit pump serves the whole queue, making the shortage visible through a normal roadside scene.
art.note: Muted industrial palette, cool evening light, calm but strained mood.

stories.headline: Revolut begins limited rollout of euro stablecoin to selected users
stories.dek: The new token, EURR, is being issued by Bridge and has started with customers in three countries.
paragraphs: Revolut has started offering EURR, a euro-denominated stablecoin, to selected customers in three countries. The token is issued by Bridge, a regulated company. The rollout is limited for now, which suggests Revolut is testing demand, operations and compliance before making the product available more widely.

A stablecoin is a digital token designed to hold a fixed value, in this case one euro. It can be used to move money on crypto rails without the price swings seen in bitcoin or ether. Bridge reportedly has about €374 of EURR outstanding, far below Circle’s roughly €394.5 million of EURC.

It is not yet clear which three countries are included, how many customers can use EURR, or what they can do with it inside Revolut. The timing of a wider launch is also unknown. The tiny amount outstanding so far means the product remains very small and early.
stories.changes: Some Revolut users may get a new way to hold or move euro value on crypto infrastructure.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean stablecoins have become mainstream money, and most Revolut customers will see no immediate difference.

cover.hook: Revolut opened its new euro stablecoin to selected users in three countries

art.label: Editorial surrealism
art.concept: Draw a clear glass euro coin tray on a bank counter, but instead of coins it holds a thin layer of still water shaped into perfect round discs. At one end, a single new disc is being lifted carefully with metal tongs, while the rest of the tray remains almost empty. No text or lettering anywhere in the scene.
art.note: Cool, restrained palette; precise light with a quiet financial mood.
